posts.title: DC+ A new operating system that sits comfortably between DC and DCC
posts.description: DC+ by MR Innovations Ltd is new operating system lets modellers record a train movement by hand and then replay it, complete with stops, reversals, points and signals – without converting their layouts to DCC. For model railway enthusiasts who enjoy hands-on operation but would sometimes like their layout to run itself, a two-man team of retired electronics engineers has developed an intriguing alternative to full digital conversion. DC+ is designed for conventional DC layouts. The idea is straightforward: drive a train through a chosen sequence, record what happens, and then let the controller repeat it. That can include changes of speed and direction, pauses, and the operation of points and signals where the appropriate accessory boards are fitted. According to co-developer Phil Williams, a routine can be recorded for up to 15 minutes. posts.title: First fare-paying passengers to use railway after union dispute stalled opening
posts.description: The first passengers will use East West Rail this weekend, almost two years after its opening was delayed by a trade union dispute. Credit: East West Rail Trains with fare-paying passengers on board are yet to use the line between Oxford and Milton Keynes because of a disagreement over whether the operator will employ guards on the route. The dispute continues, so the Chiltern Railways trains intended for the new track are not up and running. But Great Western Railway (GWR) trains on diversion between South Wales, Bristol and London will use the line while engineering works take place in the capital. Builders handed the line over to Network Rail in December 2024. Chiltern Railways, which was a private company until nationalisation in September this year, was chosen to run the trains in March 2025. posts.title: Eurostar services cancelled amid ‘unexpected’ staff strike
posts.description: Eurostar services between London and Paris have been cancelled due to unexpected strike action, the company has said. Sergii Figurnyi / Shutterstock.com The 7.01am, 8.01am and 12.31pm trains from London St Pancras to Paris Gare du Nord on Wednesday were listed as cancelled because of the strike on the Eurostar website. In a status update on its website, the company said: “Due to unexpected industrial action today, we are experiencing cancellations and severe disruption to our trains between London and Paris today. It is understood that Eurostar is currently in annual pay negotiations with a union in France during which no decision has been made and discussions remain ongoing. “Other routes might be impacted too. We advise you to change your journey for a different date of travel.” A Eurostar spokesperson said the company had been informed of the industrial action “overnight”.
